sentences.text: Researchers selected patients with confirmed disease progression who had at least two PET scans taken within a six-month window to measure static metrics like tumor-to-brain ratios and metabolic tumor volume, as well as how these values changed over time. When the disease progressed, the average tumor-to-brain ratio, maximum tumor-to-brain ratio, and metabolic tumor volume all increased significantly.

While the average and maximum tumor-to-brain ratios rose by only 4% and 17% respectively, the metabolic tumor volume expanded by 182%. For patients with unclear scan results, using a rule that required a 40% or greater increase in metabolic tumor volume improved the detection of progression to 89%. This longitudinal approach resulted in a 14% higher rate of correctly identifying disease progression compared to looking at a single scan.
